title: The Students Who Stole a King's Stone

sections.name: Hook
lines: sd_hook
On Christmas Day, 1950, a group of students broke into Westminster Abbey, and stole a stone that kings had been crowned over for centuries.
sd_title
This is the theft of the Stone of Destiny.

sections.name: The stone
lines: sd_stone
The Stone of Destiny, also called the Stone of Scone, was once used to crown Scotland's kings.
sd_chair
Over six hundred years ago, England's King Edward the First took it to London, and built it into the coronation chair in Westminster Abbey.

sections.name: The plan
lines: sd_students
Four students from Glasgow decide to take it back to Scotland. They drive to London just before Christmas.

sections.name: Christmas night
lines: sd_break
In the early hours of Christmas morning, they force their way into the abbey and drag the heavy stone out of the chair.
sd_crack
Then disaster. The stone falls, and breaks into two pieces.
sd_escape
They carry the pieces out to their cars, and drive off into the night. Britain wakes up to a Christmas mystery.

sections.name: The hunt
lines: sd_border
Police set up roadblocks on the border between England and Scotland, for the first time in four hundred years.
sd_hidden
But the stone is already hidden. Back in Scotland, a stonemason secretly repairs it.

sections.name: The ending
lines: sd_arbroath
In April 1951, the stone turns up at Arbroath Abbey, draped in a Scottish flag. The students were never prosecuted.
sd_outro
Decades later, the stone was officially returned to Scotland. Was it theft, or a homecoming? Follow for more true crime, animated.
